texts.facts: 1. Both the parties are aggrieved by the order passed by the learned Presiding Officer, District Tribunal, Ranchi, in Reference Case No.05 of 1997 and have filed the instant writ petitions. 2. The parties shall be referred to as the "Management" and the "Workman-Union" hereinafter. Neutral Citation No. 2025:Jhhc:32586 3. The Workman-Union claimed that its workmen had been working permanent and continuous nature of job in the Canteen run by the Management for the benefits of its employees working in the Bokaro Steel Plant. All the concerned workmen were working in the Canteen under the direct control and supervision of the Management since long but the Management illegally and arbitrary terminated their services with effect from 29.07.1979. The Workman-Union challenged the illegal termination of services of the concerned workmen which was first referred before the Labour Court, Bokaro Steel City and numbered as Reference Case No.04 of 1990. The Workman-Union thereafter filed a petition for impleading the Bokaro Steel Plant as a necessary party in the Labour Court to the Reference and it was thereafter the Management was impleaded. Bokaro Steel Plant vs Their Workman Represented By Bokaro ... on 30 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117549785/ 2 4. The Management filed a review petition before the Labour Court against the order of impleadment, but the same was rejected vide order dated 27.01.1994. The Management thereafter moved the Patna High Court (Ranchi Bench) by filing a writ petition challenging the aforesaid order of the Labour Court which was registered as C.W.J.C. No.1004 of 1994 and the High Court confirmed the order passed by the Labour Court. 5. Thereafter, the Management moved the Labour Court claiming that since the total number of employees in the order of reference was more than 100, therefore, it should not be referred to the Tribunal. This Neutral Citation No. 2025:JHHC:32586 contention was accepted by the Labour Court and accordingly the order was passed and the matter was referred to the Tribunal at Ranchi and numbered as Reference Case No.05 of 1987. 6. The workmen again filed a petition before the learned Tribunal for impleading the Management i.e. the Bokaro Steel Plant, as a necessary party to the reference and accordingly the Tribunal vide its order dated 15.02.2000 impleaded the Management as a necessary party to the reference. 8. The Management thereafter preferred L.P.A. No. 81 of 2002, but the same was dismissed vide order dated 15.12.2003. 9. The said order was assailed before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, but the Management has not disclosed the order so passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. 10. The Workman-Union examined the workmen, namely, Raju Mahato, as a witness who stated on oath that at the time of appointment, all the concerned workmen were asked to give three passport size photographs and the Management undertook medical examination and after medical examination they were appointed. He further stated that owner of the Canteen is the Bokaro Steel Plant, furniture was also provided by the Bokaro Steel Plant, and even the water and electricity Neutral Citation No. 2025:JHHC:32586 had been provided by the Bokaro Steel Plant. Moreover, the food prepared in that Canteen is only for the employees working in the factory and the services are being supervised by the Canteen Supervisor of Bokaro Steel Plant and they are working under the direct control and supervision of the Management. 11. The Management, on the other hand, examined three witnesses, namely, Sudhir Kumar Das (MW.1), Dharmaraj Singh (MW.2) and Md. Alam (MW.3) who have supported the case of the Management by stating that the workmen were employees of the contractors and the Management had only provided space, furniture and water & electricity connection, whereas, for all other purposes, the employees were employed/engaged by the contractors. 13. As regards the workmen, it is stated that the Workman-Union has filed the instant writ petition, i.e. W.P. (L) No.3585 of 2009, seeking a direction to the Management to reinstate the concerned workmen with full back-wages with effect from 29.07.1979 as per the award dated 25.08.2008 (pronounced on 13.10.2008) which actually is the relief granted by the learned Labour Court and this Court really fails to Neutral Citation No. 2025:JHHC:32586 understand how such writ petition seeking enforcement of the award is maintainable. 14. Accordingly, W.P. (L) No.3585 of 2009 is ordered to be dismissed as not maintainable. 15. Adverting to W.P. (L) No.1716 of 2009, the same has been filed by the Management for the grant of the following reliefs:- "For the issuance of an appropriate writ/writs, order/orders, direction/directions or a writ in the nature of Certiorari for quashing of the award dated 25th August, 2008 passed by the Learned Presiding Officer, Industrial Tribunal, Ranchi passed in Reference Case No. 5 of 1997 whereby and whereunder reference has been answered positively in favour of the work workman by holding the termination of 128 workman who are contract workers as not proper and justified and has been directed to be reinstated with full backwages w.e.f. 29.7.79." 16.
texts.arguments: 25. The issue involved in the instant lis has been time & again raised before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of canteens run by steel plants Neutral Citation No. 2025:JHHC:32586 and the matter has been dealt with in detail by Hon'ble Three Judges of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Balwant Rai Saluja and Another v. Air India Limited and Others, (2014) 9 SCC 407, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that workers, to be called the employees of the factory for all purposes, they would need to satisfy the test of employer-employee relationship and it must be shown that the employer exercises absolute and effective control over the said workers. 26. The judgment was rendered on account of there being a difference of opinion by two Hon'ble Judges by a referral order dated 13.11.2013 and the question before the Bench came - whether the workmen engaged in statutory canteens, through a contractor, could be treated as employees of the principal establishment? It was held that to be called the employees of the factory for all purposes, the workmen need to satisfy the test of employer-employee relationship and it must be shown that the employer exercises absolute and effective control over the said workers. The said case was the case of canteen run by a contractor for employees of Air India Limited and the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:- Bokaro Steel Plant vs Their Workman Represented By Bokaro ... on 30 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117549785/ 5 "65. Thus, it can be concluded that the relevant factors to be taken into consideration to establish an employer-employee relationship would include, inter alia: (i) who appoints the workers; (ii) who pays the salary/remuneration; (iii) who has the authority to dismiss; (iv) who can take disciplinary action; (v) whether there is continuity of service; and Neutral Citation No. 2025:JHHC:32586 (vi) extent of control and supervision i.e. whether there exists complete control and supervision. This is so held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Balwant Rai Saluja and Another v. Air India Limited and Others' case (supra). It shall be apt to reproduce the relevant observations as contained in paragraphs 16, 17, 28, 29, 30, 41, 76 and 90 which read as under:- "16. Section 46 of the 1948 Act statutorily places an obligation on the occupier of a factory to provide and maintain a canteen in the factory where more than two hundred and fifty workers are employed. The provision reads as under: "46.Canteens.--(1) The State Government may make rules requiring that in any specified factory wherein more than two hundred and fifty workers are ordinarily employed, a canteen or canteens shall be provided and maintained by the occupier for the use of the workers. Neutral Citation No. 2025:JHHC:32586 (2) Without prejudice in the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for-- (a) the date by which such canteen shall be provided; (b) the standard in respect of construction, accommodation, furniture and other equipment of the canteen; (c) the foodstuffs to be served therein and the charges which may be made therefor; (d) the constitution of a Managing Committee for the canteen and representation of the workers in the management of the canteen; (dd) the items of expenditure in the running of the canteen which are not to be taken into account in fixing the cost of foodstuffs and which shall be borne by the employer; (e) the delegation to the Chief Inspector, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, of the power to make rules under clause (c)." 17. This Court is in agreement with the principle laid down in Indian Petrochemicals case [Indian Petrochemicals Corpn. Ltd. v. Shramik Sena, (1999) 6 SCC 439 : 1999 SCC (L&S) 1138] wherein it was held that: (SCC p. 449, para 22) Neutral Citation No. 2025:JHHC:32586 "22. ... the workmen of a statutory canteen would be the workmen of the establishment for the purpose of the 1948 Act only and not for all other purposes." As has been observed in Indian Petrochemicals case , (1999) 6 SCC 439 , the 1948 Act does not govern the rights of employees with reference to recruitment, seniority, promotion, retirement benefits, etc. 90. In terms of the above, the reference is answered as follows: the workers engaged by a contractor to work in the statutory canteen of a Neutral Citation No. 2025:JHHC:32586 factory would be the workers of the said factory, but only for the purposes of the 1948 Act, and not for other purposes, and further for the said workers, to be called the employees of the factory for all purposes, they would need to satisfy the test of employer-employee relationship and it must be shown that the employer exercises absolute and effective control over the said workers."
